data.content_ref: inline:The target's causal story for the cross-city modulation is internally self-contradictory and undermines its own mechanism. The claim asserts that the nocturnal gap is largest in arid cities because rural land lacks moisture for latent cooling, so the countryside cools slowly. But the mechanism text simultaneously states that in humid environments, rural vegetation provides strong latent heat cooling after sunset — which would make the countryside cool *faster* and thus enlarge the gap, the exact opposite of the asserted effect (that humid cities show a *smaller* gap). The claim also attributes humid rural cooling to irrigation and green space, which are urban features, not rural baseline properties, conflating the urban oasis with the rural reference and making the aridity-vs-humidity contrast incoherent. The target even flags this exact flaw in its own counterconditions (irrigated urban green space could reverse the gap), yet never resolves the tension. Thus the target fails to provide a single coherent mechanism for why the gap is larger in some cities than others.
